title: UpANNS: Enhancing Billion-Scale ANNS Efficiency with Real-World PIM Architecture
problem: Billion-scale ANNS inefficient: CPU bottlenecked by bandwidth, GPU underutilizes resources; poor energy efficiency
motivation: AI systems need efficient billion-scale ANNS for RAG-LLMs and real-time recommendation serving
method: UpANNS positions data intelligently within a Processing-In-Memory chip (where processors are built into the memory itself to eliminate slow data movement) to speed up similarity searches across billions of entries. It dynamically adjusts computational resources based on real-time needs, and encodes data so similar items sit near each other (called co-occurrence optimization), making lookups faster. Finally, it eliminates weak candidate matches early on, so the system only fully computes scores for the most promising results.
key_novelty: UpANNS achieves near-linear performance scaling for billion-entry similarity search on Processing-In-Memory chips, delivering 4.3 times higher query throughput than the standard Faiss system and 2.3 times better energy efficiency than GPU approaches.
contributions: 4.3x QPS gain over CPU, GPU-matched performance with better efficiency
limitations: Specific to UPMEM architecture; billion-scale focus limits applicability to smaller datasets
